newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening softer, focused on techs.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening softer, focused on techs.

text.p: Wall Street shares were expected to trend down modestly at the market open on Wednesday, after yesterday's poor showing in the technology sector, analysts said.

Technology stocks, which slumped after several profit warnings on Tuesday, could feel renewed but fainter pressure at the start of the session and blue chips, which posted moderate gains yesterday, might experience mild profit-taking.
"Stocks could see a little downdraft in the beginning," said Joseph Battipaglio, chief investment officer at Gruntal.
"The techs were pretty ugly yesterday," he said. "Stocks across the board could come under pressure, with the Dow and the S&P seeing some profit-taking, though nothing material."
The Dow industrial average rose 22.75 points on Tuesday to close at 7312.15. Big board stocks were helped by a decline in bond yields, which boosted financial stocks.

But Nasdaq, heavily weighted with technology stocks, fell 1.4 percent or 19.88 points to 1384.91. Earnings warnings from disk drive maker Seagate Technology Inc and networking company Cabletron Systems Inc sparked the selloff.
The broader market performance today would depend on whether investors continued to dump technology stocks, or used the recent weakness as a buying opportunity, analysts said.
"It's a mixed bag, coming off of a couple of mixed days," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities said. "The key is what technology will do."

Gruntal's Battipaglio said: "The question is whether investors will use the opportunites presented by declines in Intel, Seagate and Bay Networks. If we see demand, that could put confidence back in the market."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was trading up 0.50 points at 843.60 on Wednesday.

Among Wednesday's technology-related events, Oracle Corp Chief Executive Larry Ellison and Time Warner Inc TWX.N Vice Chairman Ted Turner will deliver a joint keynote address to the Spring Comdex show in Atlanta.
Bear Stearns will also hold a press briefing with technology analysts ahead of its annual technology conference.
If bond yields continued to perform well, interest-rate sensitive stocks and the overall stock market would draw some support, analysts said.
The long bond was down 7/32 at a 6.89 percent yield.
U.S. factory orders for April were due out at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT and could provide some direction to bonds. They were forecast to be up 0.8 percent versus a previous decline of 1.6 percent.
Japan's Nikkei-225 index finished up 48.40 points at 20611.56.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 24.1 points at 4581.9. U.S. stocks were mixed in quiet trading in London.
The dollar edged up against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 116.35/45 yen. In Europe, the dollar was at 1.7295/05 marks.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reported Starbucks Corp stock, which had suffered due to a rise in coffee-bean prices, might be hampered by increased competition in the coffee-shop market.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column said U.S. stock markets appeared to be moving away from quoting share prices in fractions, using dollars and cents instead.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
